findings.summary: A FOURTH limit exists, is pinned, and is missing from the list -- and it DUPLICATES, so 'the one case that duplicates' at :98-99 is false against the tree
findings.detail: The bare v0 checkpoint slot. ChainReplay.java:341 states it verbatim in src/main: 'for a pod whose only record is a bare slot, a replay crossing a takeover is treated as fresh and applied twice'. Checkpoint.decode yields PodState.bare(watermark) for a v0 object -- no incarnation, no pointer -- so ChainReplay.java:349 skips it, the checkpoint still bounds the walk, and that pod's deltas are never read. It is PINNED, better than limit 1 is: DedupAcrossTakeoverTest.aBAREV0CheckpointSlotLeavesItsPodUNPROTECTED_AndThatIsRecorded:356 drives a real takeover and asserts deltasCarrying(store, "seg/0").isEqualTo(2). It has its own owner, M5.22, marked done WITH the gap open until v0 checkpoints age out of retention. It is a different mechanism from limit 1 (limit 1 is Checkpoint.pods being keyed by podId so only the latest incarnation survives; this is a slot that cannot be keyed or followed at all), so it is not covered by the first bullet. Failure scenario: a caller or a future author reads this contract -- the copy a caller hits -- and concludes that outside the narrow superseded-incarnation window a takeover-crossing retry can only cost an error, never two copies of the same records at two offsets. During any rolling upgrade with v0 checkpoints still in retention that is wrong, and I2 is broken exactly where the javadoc says it cannot be. Two further sites carry the same false exclusivity and must move with it: backlog.md:43's done cell ('the superseded incarnation the single case that duplicates', and 'THE THREE ... verified against the code rather than listed'), and M5/SPEC.md:328, where acceptance criterion 3 delegates its whole exception list to this enumeration ('the limits M5.34 enumerates are all cases where a retry crossing a takeover is appended or refused rather than answered. Do not mark this verified without reading that row') -- so criterion 3 would be signed off against a list short by one, which is the fourth successive short enumeration this row exists to stop. A FIFTH candidate, weaker but on the same topic and also absent: IdempotencyWindow.answer's other refusal branch, 'points at sequence N of epoch E, which holds no delta' (IdempotencyWindow.java:259-262), whose own comment says it is 'UNREACHABLE UNTIL THE WINDOW IS INHERITED ... A pointer INHERITED from a predecessor's checkpoint can outlive its delta, which is where this refusal starts to matter' -- i.e. a limit that exists only when crossing a takeover, with a distinct message and no test asserting it (grep for 'holds no delta' finds no test).
findings.failure_scenario: A rolling upgrade leaves v0 checkpoints inside the retention window. A pod whose only checkpoint record is a bare v0 slot has its takeover-crossing replay treated as fresh and committed a second time -- DedufAcrossTakeoverTest asserts deltasCarrying == 2 today -- while this contract javadoc, the copy a caller hits, says the superseded incarnation is the ONLY case that duplicates. An operator debugging doubled records at two offsets (an I2 violation) reads the contract, sees the pod never restarted, and rules out duplication; and M5/SPEC.md:328 signs off acceptance criterion 3 against this list, so the criterion is marked with an exception list short by one for the fourth time.

findings.summary: The M5.25 COUNT is left standing in src/main one file away: 'a replay crossing a takeover is caught, with the one limit that a checkpoint remembers a pod's LATEST incarnation only'
findings.detail: The task is to enumerate the limits ONCE and make the javadoc agree. Sequencer.java now names three; IdempotencyWindow.java:43 still counts ONE, over the same property and in the same words M5.25 used ('with the one limit that a checkpoint remembers a pod's LATEST incarnation only'). Sequencer's contract links straight into this class and this is the class that implements the window, so a reader following the seam from the fixed copy arrives at the stale one. Failure scenario: exactly the history the row records, one more time -- the next author reads IdempotencyWindow, believes one limit exists, and writes a fourth wrong count; or a reviewer greps src/main for the limit statement, finds two src/main copies that disagree, and cannot tell which is authoritative. Renaming the fix 'named rather than counted' does not help while a bare count of the same thing survives in the adjacent file. (IdempotencyWindow.java:102's 'ONE INCARNATION PER POD ... a stated limit' is fine -- it names one limit, it does not count them.)
findings.failure_scenario: The next author follows Sequencer's seam into IdempotencyWindow -- the class that implements the window -- reads line 43's 'with the one limit that a checkpoint remembers a pod's LATEST incarnation only', and writes a fourth wrong count, or trusts it over the new three-item list. Two src/main statements of the same property now disagree and nothing says which is authoritative, which is the exact defect (M5.25 'one', M5.27 'two', review 'three') this task exists to end.

findings.summary: Bullet 2's stated mechanism and its named pin are different things: the test cited replays the SAME segmentKey from below the pointer -- i.e. bullet 3's mechanism -- while the different-segment rule it describes is pinned by a test the list does not name
findings.detail: The bullet says 'only the triple AND the same segmentKey answer one, so resending a triple under a different segment is refused permanently for that flushSeq' and cites SequencerDedupTest.aReplayThePointedDeltaDoesNotCarryIsREFUSED. That test (SequencerDedupTest.java:115-131) commits zero = (poda,i1,0,seg/0), then (poda,i1,1,seg/1), then replays `zero` VERBATIM -- same segmentKey -- and it is refused because the single pointer now names flushSeq 1's delta. No different segment key is ever submitted. Its refusal is the one-pointer-per-incarnation staleness, which is precisely what bullet 3 (lines 88-93) names, so as written the list spends two of its three entries on one mechanism in two configurations (without and with a takeover) while the genuinely distinct segmentKey rule is described but not pinned. That rule IS pinned, elsewhere and unmentioned: SequencerDedupTest.aSegmentMatchingOnlyPARTOfTheTripleAnswersNOTHING:254-259, the `otherKey` assertion over IdempotencyWindow.answers. Failure scenario: someone deletes or weakens that `otherKey` assertion, then greps the contract for a pin covering 'a triple under a different segment key' -- bullet 2 names a test that stays green under that deletion, so the rule looks pinned and is not, and answering a retry with another flush's offsets becomes reachable with the javadoc still asserting it cannot. This also breaks the paragraph's own promise at lines 72-73 ('each of these carries the test that holds it so the list is checkable rather than asserted') on the entry it is most likely to be checked on. Related and same site: the segmentKey rule is now stated twice in one javadoc, at 82-87 and again at 102-110, 15 lines apart in near-identical prose -- a second copy to drift, in a commit whose mandate is to enumerate ONCE.
findings.failure_scenario: Someone deletes or weakens the `otherKey` assertion in SequencerDedupTest.aSegmentMatchingOnlyPARTOfTheTripleAnswersNOTHING:254-259. A reviewer greps the contract for a pin covering 'a triple resent under a different segment key', finds bullet 2, and runs the test it names -- which replays the SAME segmentKey and stays green under that deletion. The rule looks pinned and is not, and IdempotencyWindow.answers can then answer a retry with another flush's offsets while this javadoc asserts it cannot.

findings.summary: The cited test name is split across a line inside {@code}, so the citation is not findable by grep
findings.detail: Lines 92-93 read `{@code DedupAcrossTakeoverTest.aReplayFromBELOWThePointerIsREFUSED_NotApplied` / ` * Twice}`. Verified: `grep -rn aReplayFromBELOWThePointerIsREFUSED_NotAppliedTwice` over the tree returns DedupAcrossTakeoverTest.java:211 and backlog.md:43 and NOT this javadoc; it also renders as a name with a space in it. Failure scenario: the test is renamed or moved, the author sweeps references by grepping the old name, this citation does not match, and the contract javadoc is left naming a test that no longer exists -- the staleness class this row exists to close. The wrap buys nothing: unbroken, the line is 92 characters, and line 39 of this same file is already 113.
